macro_regime_hint.label: supportive
macro_regime_hint.note: Deterministic hint only — the agent must form its own regime view.

no_trade_reason: Macro is mixed-to-cautious, not clean-supportive: CPI YoY reaccelerated 2.66%->4.27% with the 10Y rising 4.34->4.55, a combination that specifically pressures multiples on high-P/E AI/semi names even though credit spreads (2.7), VIX (16.9) and NFCI (-0.52) show a risk-on tape. Against that backdrop the entire universe is extended (3-month momentum +48% TXN to +231% ALAB), leaving no favorable swing entries: AMD ($545) is spiking today on an AI-alliance news pop after a +135% run (chasing); ALAB and CRDO are parabolic with ~11.3% ATR that makes a 15%-max stop pure noise; TXN ($309) is a clean business but entering 13 days before its 2026-07-22 earnings is a binary print bet I can't honestly rate >=0.60; ANET ($184.85) is the highest-quality name but sits -2.6% from its 52-week high with no pullback and its next catalyst (8/4 earnings) is ~4 weeks out, so a 2:1 requires an optimistic ~+16% target with no margin of safety. Forcing any of these to clear confidence>=0.60 and RR>=2.0 would mean backing into targets I don't believe. Holding cash ($10,000) and waiting for a pullback or post-earnings reset is the higher-expected-value action, consistent with 'fewer, better trades; proposing nothing is preferred over a mediocre setup.'

improvements.note: Added one-day price change and valuation context (P/E, EV/EBITDA) to the market scanner. The agent flagged that it could not tell a stock resting after a rally from one spiking on same-day news, and could not judge whether extended names were actually expensive. Both gaps are now closed.

watchlist.one_line: Highest-quality compounder in the universe, but sitting at its highs with no pullback to buy.
watchlist.thoughts: Arista is the cleanest business I researched this cycle: revenue grew from $1.46B to $2.0B, net income from $492M to $814M, gross margins near 64%, and it beats steadily. Momentum is measured rather than parabolic, up 27% in three months. The problem is price: it trades 2.6% from its 52-week high with no pullback, and the next catalyst is earnings on August 4, about four weeks out. Paying the high with no margin of safety is how compounding gets hurt. I want a dip or a post-earnings reset.
watchlist.would_buy_at: on a pullback toward the 50-day average, or after 8/4 earnings

watchlist.one_line: Clean analog recovery story with smart-money backing, but earnings on July 22 make entry a coin flip.
watchlist.thoughts: Texas Instruments is a moderate mover, up 48% in three months on an analog recovery rather than an AI parabola, with lower volatility than the rest of the universe. D1 Capital holds a $340M position per the latest 13F. The hard catalyst is earnings on July 22. Buying thirteen days before a binary print is a bet on the quarter, not an investment thesis, and I cannot honestly claim 60% confidence in a coin flip. After the print, this becomes very interesting either way.
watchlist.would_buy_at: after 7/22 earnings, on confirmation or an overreaction dip

watchlist.one_line: Great story, but it spiked on same-day alliance news after a 135% three-month run; chasing spikes breaks compounding.
watchlist.thoughts: AMD topped my scanner this cycle, but it was up over 5% on the day I looked, driven by AI Infrastructure Alliance headlines, after already more than doubling in three months. It trades at roughly 182x trailing and 41x forward earnings, so the multiple assumes a lot goes right. Buying the literal news spike after a double is the worst entry in the group. I want to see how it digests this move; a few weeks of consolidation would change my mind.
watchlist.would_buy_at: after a multi-week consolidation or a 10-15% digestion of the news pop

watchlist.one_line: Data center cooling pure-play with accelerating revenue; researching whether the ramp justifies a position.
watchlist.thoughts: Vertiv sells the power and cooling gear every AI data center needs, and its quarterly revenue trend shows the buildout is real. It did not make my top setups this cycle on price structure, but the fundamental engine is exactly the multi-quarter story this portfolio wants to own. I need to finish underwriting the valuation against its own history and find an entry that is not extended.
watchlist.would_buy_at: pending deeper valuation work and a stable technical base

watchlist.one_line: Hyper-growth connectivity name, up 142% in three months; too parabolic to touch until volatility cools.
watchlist.thoughts: Credo makes the high-speed connections between AI chips, and the growth is spectacular. But the stock is parabolic with daily swings near 11%, which means any responsible stop-loss gets hit by pure noise. Names like this eventually give a calmer entry after their first real correction, and that is when the risk becomes manageable. Watching, not chasing.
watchlist.would_buy_at: after a correction brings volatility down to a manageable range
